stories.title: Preserve the source beside the transcription
stories.body: Editorial demo copy: keep a stable source reference, transcription status, script profile, and review notes with each digital text.

workshops.title: Lipi OS Orientation
workshops.subtitle: Find your way around language, script, and study tools.
workshops.objective: Introduce the Lipi OS learning areas and help participants set a study focus without conflating a language with its writing system.

sessions.title: Welcome and learning goals
sessions.activity: Set expectations and identify what participants want to learn.

sessions.title: Navigate the Lipi OS concept
sessions.activity: Tour the language selector, script registry, course links, and reference areas.

sessions.title: Choose a study focus
sessions.activity: Select a language and a script record; note where the two differ.

sessions.title: Read a study outline
sessions.activity: Examine context, writing conventions, cited examples, and review status.

sessions.title: Try a guided learning task
sessions.activity: Complete a short observation and reflection exercise using reviewed material.

sessions.title: Review and next steps
sessions.activity: Record open questions and a personal follow-up goal.

checks: Language and script are clearly distinguished in labels and examples.
Navigation, selected-language state, and learning links work with keyboard and assistive technology.
All cited examples show source and review status.
qa.evidence: A learner study goal and one source-linked observation.

workshops.title: Language vs. Script
workshops.subtitle: Separate speech, language identity, and writing systems.
workshops.objective: Build a shared vocabulary for languages, scripts, transliteration, transcription, and historical writing styles.

sessions.title: Opening examples
sessions.activity: Compare several ways a language or phrase can be represented.

sessions.title: Language concepts
sessions.activity: Discuss spoken and written forms, language varieties, and naming choices.

sessions.title: Script concepts
sessions.activity: Identify writing systems, script families, direction, and historical styles.

sessions.title: Representation terms
sessions.activity: Distinguish translation, transcription, transliteration, and rendering.

sessions.title: Classify sample records
sessions.activity: Sort reviewed examples into language, script, style, and encoding fields.

sessions.title: Recap and questions
sessions.activity: Capture terms that need clarification or specialist review.

checks: Language, script, style, direction, and encoding fields are not conflated.
Terms for translation, transcription, transliteration, and rendering are consistently defined.
Classification examples are reviewed and include an answer key.
qa.evidence: A completed classification exercise with corrections noted.

workshops.title: Explore a Script
workshops.subtitle: Read a script record through form, direction, and evidence.
workshops.objective: Practice observing a selected script using cited, reviewed examples while making uncertainty and historical context visible.

sessions.title: Scope and source boundary
sessions.activity: Choose an approved script record and identify what the session can and cannot claim.

sessions.title: Script profile
sessions.activity: Review region, period labels, script name, and language distinctions.

sessions.title: Direction and visual forms
sessions.activity: Observe writing direction and recurring visual features in reviewed samples.

sessions.title: Read a cited example
sessions.activity: Work through a short example with references and specialist-approved notes.

sessions.title: Compare editions or styles
sessions.activity: Record visible variation without treating it as a universal rule.

sessions.title: Reflection and open questions
sessions.activity: Write an observation, a source question, and a next research step.

checks: Script name, region, period, direction, and language relationship cite reliable sources.
Examples identify edition or object context and receive qualified review.
Uncertain or disputed readings are marked instead of silently resolved.
qa.evidence: A short annotated observation with citation and an open research question.

workshops.title: Reading and Writing Practice
workshops.subtitle: Build a careful first practice routine for a reviewed script.
workshops.objective: Introduce a repeatable practice sequence using approved fonts, examples, and learning materials for one selected script.

sessions.title: Materials and setup
sessions.activity: Check the approved font, keyboard or worksheet, and access needs.

sessions.title: Sound and form orientation
sessions.activity: Introduce only the reviewed signs and values included in the lesson pack.

sessions.title: Guided form practice
sessions.activity: Practice selected forms with instructor feedback and accessible alternatives.

sessions.title: Word or phrase practice
sessions.activity: Read or write a short, sourced example suited to the chosen script.

sessions.title: Peer review
sessions.activity: Compare attempts against the approved reference and note ambiguities.

sessions.title: Practice plan
sessions.activity: Set a realistic follow-up routine and list support needs.

checks: Fonts, sign forms, sound values, and sample readings are checked by a qualified reviewer.
Keyboard/input method instructions match the named device and include a non-digital alternative.
Practice materials support readable contrast, scalable text, and accessible feedback.
qa.evidence: A reviewed practice sheet or equivalent accessible exercise.

workshops.title: Manuscripts and Book Research
workshops.subtitle: Turn a reading question into a source-aware search plan.
workshops.objective: Practice locating catalogued books and manuscript records while tracking edition, access, rights, and provenance details.

sessions.title: Frame a research question
sessions.activity: Define a topic, language, script, period, or text family to investigate.

sessions.title: Search catalogues
sessions.activity: Use catalogue fields and external collection links to discover records.

sessions.title: Compare editions and metadata
sessions.activity: Record title variants, editors, dates, identifiers, and description gaps.

sessions.title: Access and rights check
sessions.activity: Check access conditions, reuse rights, and restrictions at the source.

sessions.title: Build a source log
sessions.activity: Create a bibliographic record with retrieval notes and confidence labels.

sessions.title: Share findings and gaps
sessions.activity: Present one useful record and one unresolved research question.

checks: Bibliographic fields distinguish title, creator, edition, date, identifier, and catalogue record.
External links are checked and access or reuse terms are recorded at the source.
Research notes retain provenance and distinguish verified facts from catalogue gaps.
qa.evidence: A source log with retrieval date, rights/access note, and confidence labels.

workshops.title: Inscriptions and Epigraphy
workshops.subtitle: Describe an inscription before interpreting it.
workshops.objective: Introduce a disciplined workflow for recording inscription context, visual observations, readings, and uncertainty from authorized sources.

sessions.title: Epigraphy and evidence
sessions.activity: Review the difference between object context, visual description, reading, and interpretation.

sessions.title: Record provenance and context
sessions.activity: Capture source, collection, catalogue reference, and permission status.

sessions.title: Describe visible features
sessions.activity: Write neutral observations using an authorized image or published record.

sessions.title: Transcription workflow
sessions.activity: Compare a published reading with the source record and document conventions.

sessions.title: Mark ambiguity and damage
sessions.activity: Use explicit uncertainty notes instead of silently filling gaps.

sessions.title: Ethics, access, and sensitive data
sessions.activity: Discuss permissions, cultural protocols, and limits on location disclosure.

sessions.title: Review and handoff
sessions.activity: Prepare a citation-ready record for specialist review.

checks: Object context, visual description, reading, and interpretation are separate record fields.
Transcription conventions and published readings are cited and reviewed by an epigraphy specialist.
Image permissions, cultural protocols, damage, uncertainty, and sensitive location data are checked.
qa.evidence: A citation-ready draft record explicitly listing unresolved readings and permissions.

workshops.title: Digital Texts: Unicode, Fonts, and Keyboards
workshops.subtitle: Understand what digital script text stores and displays.
workshops.objective: Introduce basic Unicode and input concepts while distinguishing encoded characters from their rendered glyph shapes.

sessions.title: Unicode overview
sessions.activity: Review code points, character names, and script blocks with reliable references.

sessions.title: Character and glyph
sessions.activity: Compare encoded text with font-dependent visual rendering.

sessions.title: Keyboard and input methods
sessions.activity: Try an appropriate input method and record its limitations.

sessions.title: Fonts and rendering
sessions.activity: Check shaping, combining marks, direction, and device differences.

sessions.title: Normalize and export
sessions.activity: Practice safe text handling and export without losing source context.

sessions.title: Quality check
sessions.activity: Review a digital text for encoding, display, and provenance issues.

checks: Unicode code points and character names are checked against current Unicode references.
Text content is tested separately from font rendering, shaping, combining marks, and direction.
Normalization or export steps preserve the original source and provenance.
qa.evidence: A text-quality report covering encoding, rendering, input method, and provenance.

workshops.title: Transcription and Transliteration
workshops.subtitle: Make representation choices explicit and reviewable.
workshops.objective: Create a transparent representation workflow that preserves source text, conventions, ambiguity, and reviewer decisions.

sessions.title: Define the terms
sessions.activity: Distinguish transcription, transliteration, translation, and editorial normalization.

sessions.title: Describe the source text
sessions.activity: Record source edition, script, language label, and relevant limitations.

sessions.title: Select a convention
sessions.activity: Choose a documented scheme appropriate to the source and audience.

sessions.title: Align text and notes
sessions.activity: Create a small aligned example with clear editorial annotations.

sessions.title: Record uncertainty
sessions.activity: Mark damaged, disputed, or unavailable readings without guessing.

sessions.title: Review choices
sessions.activity: Compare independent work and log changes with reasons.

sessions.title: Prepare handoff
sessions.activity: Package source references, conventions, and unresolved questions.

checks: The selected convention is named, versioned where applicable, and appropriate to the source.
Aligned text retains source references and separates editorial normalization from translation.
Damaged, disputed, or unavailable readings and every revision are documented.
qa.evidence: A small aligned example with convention note, citations, and change log.

workshops.title: Language Documentation
workshops.subtitle: Plan consent-led recording and responsible return of materials.
workshops.objective: Plan a voluntary documentation activity that respects participant choices, privacy, ownership, and agreed access.

sessions.title: Consent and participant control
sessions.activity: Discuss informed consent, withdrawal, attribution, and recording choices.

sessions.title: Set a research question
sessions.activity: Narrow the purpose and identify who benefits from the work.

sessions.title: Prepare an interview plan
sessions.activity: Draft open prompts and an accessible, participant-led session plan.

sessions.title: Recording practice
sessions.activity: Practice audio setup, room tone, file naming, and a non-recorded alternative.

sessions.title: Transcription and metadata
sessions.activity: Plan language labels, translation notes, review roles, and provenance.

sessions.title: Privacy and return of materials
sessions.activity: Set access, storage, sharing, and community return expectations.

sessions.title: Reflection and safeguards
sessions.activity: Review risks, referral needs, and conditions to pause or stop.

checks: Consent, withdrawal, attribution, access, retention, and participant review are agreed before recording.
The session offers a non-recorded alternative and accessible participant-led prompts.
Files and metadata follow approved privacy, storage, sharing, and community-return plans.
qa.evidence: An approved interview plan and metadata template; recordings are not required.

workshops.title: Script and Place Atlas
workshops.subtitle: Map records with provenance and coordinate uncertainty.
workshops.audience: Researchers, educators, and digital heritage teams
workshops.objective: Build a sample map record from cited sources while avoiding unsupported site extents or disclosure of sensitive locations.

sessions.title: Spatial data orientation
sessions.activity: Review point, boundary, route, and uncertainty as different data types.

sessions.title: Choose a cited record
sessions.activity: Select a public, suitable source and document its scope.

sessions.title: Assess coordinate quality
sessions.activity: Record precision, datum, source date, and verification status.

sessions.title: Create a map record
sessions.activity: Add metadata, citations, and a clear note about what the marker represents.

sessions.title: Sensitive data review
sessions.activity: Apply access controls or omit data that could expose protected locations.

sessions.title: Quality assurance
sessions.activity: Check attribution, coordinate validity, and interpretation limits.

sessions.title: Review and publish decision
sessions.activity: Decide whether the record is ready for a public map or needs review.

checks: Coordinates include source, date, datum/CRS, precision, and verification status.
The map marker describes the source record and does not imply unsupported site boundaries or certainty.
Sensitive locations, attribution, keyboard access, and non-map alternatives are reviewed.
qa.evidence: A cited map-record draft with coordinate-quality and sensitivity notes.

workshops.title: Build a Script Study Outline
workshops.subtitle: Co-design a reviewable lesson plan for one script.
workshops.audience: Educators, subject specialists, and learning designers
workshops.objective: Draft a lesson sequence with sourced material, practice and assessment plans, and named scholarly review needs.

sessions.title: Set a learning outcome
sessions.activity: Write one achievable, assessable outcome for a defined learner group.

sessions.title: Describe learner context
sessions.activity: Record prior knowledge, language needs, access requirements, and constraints.

sessions.title: Select and audit sources
sessions.activity: Choose credible references and identify permissions or content gaps.

sessions.title: Sequence the lesson
sessions.activity: Draft an opening, explanation, guided example, practice, and reflection.

sessions.title: Design an activity
sessions.activity: Create a low-risk exercise using only reviewed forms and examples.

sessions.title: Plan assessment
sessions.activity: Define a feedback method that tests the stated learning outcome.

sessions.title: Peer and specialist review
sessions.activity: Collect questions for language, script, accessibility, and rights review.

sessions.title: Revise and track gaps
sessions.activity: Publish a draft outline with owner, review status, and next actions.

checks: Activities and assessment align with a clear learning outcome and learner context.
Sources, permissions, accessibility needs, and specialist-review gaps are recorded.
Outline version, reviewer, owner, and next actions are tracked before publication.
qa.evidence: A reviewed lesson outline with assessment plan and unresolved-gap register.

workshops.title: Advanced Water Management Solutions by Ancient Sciences
workshops.focus: Compare documented water systems with modern hydrology, GIS, monitoring and conservation design.
workshops.researcher: Water-heritage researcher; evidence and source-pack lead
index: 1 · Reading water in the landscape — catchments, seasonality and settlement patterns (1.5 h)
2 · Documented systems and their contexts — wells, tanks, channels and storage (2 h)
3 · Evidence lab — source quality, dating, function and uncertainty (1.5 h)
4 · Modern hydrology tools — flow, infiltration, water balance and GIS (2 h)
5 · Monitoring and stewardship — water quality, maintenance and community governance (2 h)
6 · Design studio — a testable, site-specific water resilience concept (3 h)

workshops.title: Symbols, Letters and their Science
workshops.focus: Study scripts, symbols, writing systems and encoding while separating evidence from interpretation.
workshops.lecturer: Historical linguist, epigrapher or writing-systems specialist
workshops.researcher: Epigraphy researcher; image permissions and source-pack lead
index: 1 · What counts as a sign, script and text? (45 min)
2 · How writing systems are described — sign lists, direction, variants and context (75 min)
3 · Reading an inscription image — observation before interpretation (60 min)
4 · From photograph to dataset — metadata, Unicode and responsible transcription (75 min)
5 · Open questions and undeciphered corpora — what evidence can and cannot establish (45 min)
6 · Practical lab — create a cited, uncertainty-aware sign record (60 min)

workshops.title: Climate-Resilient Agriculture and Soil Futures
workshops.focus: Connect documented farming practices with current soil, weather and irrigation research.
workshops.researcher: Agricultural-history researcher; evidence and source-pack lead
index: 1 · Climate, crops and historical evidence — framing questions (1.5 h)
2 · Reading soils — texture, structure, organic matter and field notes (2 h)
3 · Farming records and material evidence — limits, dates and context (1.5 h)
4 · Resilience tools — crop diversity, water efficiency and risk mapping (2 h)
5 · Field-data practice — sampling plans, consent and safe handling (2 h)
6 · Design studio — a locally testable adaptation and evaluation plan (3 h)

workshops.title: Traditional Materials and Circular Manufacturing
workshops.focus: Study material histories alongside reuse, repair and low-waste manufacturing.
workshops.lecturer: Materials scientist, conservation specialist or circular-design practitioner
index: 1 · Material biographies — source, transformation, use and discard (1.5 h)
2 · Evidence and methods — visual study, sampling ethics and lab techniques (2 h)
3 · Claims check — provenance, dating and limits of reconstruction (1.5 h)
4 · Circularity metrics — repair, reuse, energy and life-cycle thinking (2 h)
5 · Prototype workshop — material choices and safe, low-waste making (2 h)
6 · Design review — performance, sourcing and a validation plan (3 h)

workshops.title: Architecture, Geometry and Passive Cooling
workshops.focus: Compare documented building features with present-day thermal comfort and energy analysis.
index: 1 · Climate, place and building form — setting the design question (1.5 h)
2 · Reading plans and fabric — geometry, materials and evidence (2 h)
3 · Shade, air and heat — passive-design principles and measurement (1.5 h)
4 · Survey-to-model — scaled drawings, sun paths and simple simulations (2 h)
5 · Comfort and conservation — accessibility, use and retrofit constraints (2 h)
6 · Design studio — a measured cooling proposal with assumptions stated (3 h)

workshops.title: Calendars, Sky Observation and Data Visualization
workshops.focus: Explore historical timekeeping records alongside modern astronomy and data visualization.
workshops.lecturer: Astronomer, archaeoastronomy specialist or science educator
workshops.researcher: History-of-astronomy researcher; data and citation lead
index: 1 · Observing the sky — cycles, coordinates and uncertainty (45 min)
2 · Calendars as systems — evidence, conventions and local variation (75 min)
3 · Historical records — how to read a date or observation in context (60 min)
4 · Data lab — compare a historical series with an astronomical dataset (75 min)
5 · Visual explanation — chart choices, uncertainty and accessible labels (45 min)
6 · Mini project — a reproducible, cited sky-data visualization (60 min)

workshops.title: Ancient Texts, AI and Digital Preservation
workshops.focus: Introduce digitization, OCR, searchable text and human review for historical materials.
workshops.researcher: Textual scholar or archivist; rights and metadata lead
index: 1 · Preservation first — object, image, transcription and rights (1.5 h)
2 · Preparing a corpus — metadata, script support and quality control (2 h)
3 · OCR and HTR — what models do, training data and error patterns (1.5 h)
4 · Human-in-the-loop review — transcription, confidence and correction (2 h)
5 · Search and publication — encoding, linked data and responsible access (2 h)
6 · Digital lab — evaluate a small workflow and document its limits (3 h)

workshops.title: Knowledge Systems, Evidence and Public Health
workshops.focus: Examine historical health-related texts as research sources, with modern evidence and safety boundaries.
workshops.lecturer: Public-health researcher or historian of medicine
index: 1 · Health knowledge in historical context — categories and sources (1.5 h)
2 · Texts, practice and material evidence — triangulation (2 h)
3 · Appraising claims — provenance, translation and evidential strength (1.5 h)
4 · Modern public-health evidence — study designs and causal limits (2 h)
5 · Ethics and communication — cultural respect, safety and misinformation (2 h)
6 · Case conference — write a sourced, non-clinical research brief (3 h)

workshops.title: Heritage Futures Lab: From Evidence to Prototype
workshops.focus: Develop a small concept from a documented source with citations, limits and a review plan.
workshops.researcher: Heritage researcher; source verification and evidence-review lead
index: 1 · Challenge framing and stakeholder map (2 h)
2 · Source discovery, provenance and evidence matrix (3 h)
3 · Research synthesis — findings, gaps and uncertainty (3 h)
4 · Concept generation and selection criteria (2 h)
5 · Prototype sprint — storyboard, model or service mock-up (4 h)
6 · Testing plan — users, measures, ethics and iteration (2 h)
7 · Review panel — critique, citations and claim boundaries (2 h)

priceBasis.excluded: Travel, lodging, specialist travel, taxes where applicable, and custom equipment.

events.title: Göbekli Tepe monumental structures
events.summary: UNESCO dates monumental structures at Göbekli Tepe to the Pre-Pottery Neolithic, built by hunter-gatherer communities. This is a place and architecture record, not a claim about the origin of language or writing.
events.evidenceNote: Range follows the UNESCO property description; no city or writing-system attribution is made.
events.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre · Göbekli Tepe

events.title: Early cuneiform records in Uruk
events.summary: The British Museum places the origin of cuneiform in what is now Iraq before 3200 BCE. The earliest proto-cuneiform tablets are primarily administrative; their language should not be assumed from the script alone.
events.evidenceNote: Script and language are kept separate because early tablets do not all establish a spoken-language label.
events.sourceLabel: The British Museum · How to write cuneiform

events.title: Ancient Egyptian writing traditions
events.summary: Egyptian texts were written in multiple scripts over time. Hieratic and Demotic served distinct contexts; Coptic later used a Greek-based alphabet with additional signs.
events.evidenceNote: These are historical script traditions for Egyptian, not simultaneous equivalents or a single unchanging alphabet.
events.sourceLabel: Unicode Standard · Egyptian scripts

events.title: Indus cities and undeciphered signs

trades: regional exchange · details vary by evidence

events.summary: Mohenjo-daro is an urban centre of the Indus civilization with planned streets and drainage. The Indus signs remain undeciphered; this timeline assigns them no language.
events.evidenceNote: Urban chronology is approximate. The sign corpus is not treated here as a deciphered text or language record.
events.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre · Moenjodaro

events.region: Nile Valley · Kush / Meroë · present-day Sudan
events.title: Meroitic language in two scripts
events.summary: Unicode describes Meroitic hieroglyphs and Meroitic cursive as scripts used to write Meroitic in the Nile Valley kingdom of Kush / Meroë.
events.evidenceNote: Date range is approximate and refers to attested use, not the language's origin.
events.sourceLabel: Unicode Standard · Meroitic

events.region: Gandhāra to the Tarim Basin · South/Central Asia
events.title: Gāndhārī manuscripts written in Kharoshthi
events.summary: A British Library collection described by the University of Washington contains birch-bark manuscripts in Gāndhārī written in Kharoshthi.
events.evidenceNote: Regional manuscript context; no precise route or coordinate is asserted by this record.
events.sourceLabel: University of Washington · British Library Kharoṣṭhī Fragments

events.title: Maya hieroglyphic writing at San Bartolo

languages: Mayan languages · specific reading depends on text

events.summary: A peer-reviewed report dates a sample of Maya hieroglyphic writing at San Bartolo to the Late Preclassic period.
events.evidenceNote: Site-period range, not a precise invention date for Maya writing or a one-to-one mapping to a single spoken language.
events.sourceLabel: Science / PubMed · Early Maya Writing at San Bartolo

events.dateLabel: From the 1st century BCE · routes evolved over time
events.region: Eurasian land routes and connected regions
events.title: Silk Roads trade and exchange networks

people: Merchants and travellers · generally not individually identified

events.summary: UNESCO describes Silk Roads land routes expanding from the 1st century BCE, with merchants moving goods and ideas among connected cities and regions.
events.evidenceNote: A network, not one fixed road, empire, or single start date; this broad range is an interface summary.
events.sourceLabel: UNESCO Silk Roads Programme · Merchants along land routes

events.title: Aśokan inscriptions and public texts
events.summary: Aśokan inscriptions are a source for ancient South Asian languages and scripts. The four plotted RRF atlas pins are site pointers, not the full distribution of inscriptions.
events.evidenceNote: Language labels vary by source; this entry does not supply a transcription or translation.
events.sourceLabel: UNESCO Tentative List · Rock Edicts of Ashoka

events.title: Sanskrit represented in Brahmi inscriptions
events.summary: A Unicode Brahmi encoding proposal describes Sanskrit being represented in Brahmi inscriptions from around the 2nd century CE, with additions to the script repertoire for Sanskrit use.
events.evidenceNote: Source describes attested inscription use; this is not a claim that Sanskrit or Brahmi originated at this date.
events.sourceLabel: Unicode Consortium · Brahmi proposal

events.dateLabel: early historic period · dates vary by inscription
events.region: Tamil Nadu and Sri Lanka · South Asia
events.title: Tamil-Brahmi inscriptions
events.summary: Unicode’s script history identifies Brahmi as having been used to write Tamil, while epigraphic scholarship discusses regional Tamil-Brahmi forms and their inscriptions.
events.evidenceNote: This is a script-language research link; individual inscriptions require their own dated records.
events.sourceLabel: Unicode Standard · Brahmi

events.title: Inka khipu record-keeping

trades: Recording goods, labour, census data, and administration
people: Khipucamayuq specialists · names generally not recorded

events.summary: Smithsonian sources describe khipu as knotted-cord systems used by Inka officials to record quantitative information and administer the empire.
events.evidenceNote: Catalogue as a record system, not as a fully deciphered alphabetic script; its full semantic range remains a research question.
events.sourceLabel: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian · Inka khipu

events.title: Nalanda Mahavihara as a scholastic institution
events.summary: UNESCO describes Nalanda as a monastic and scholastic establishment operating from the 5th to 13th centuries CE; the site itself includes remains from earlier periods.
events.evidenceNote: The institutional dates are separated from the site's wider archaeological date range.
events.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre · Nalanda Mahavihara

events.region: India to China; later Korea and Japan
events.title: Siddham script in East Asian Buddhist texts

languages: Sanskrit · in relevant Buddhist text traditions

events.summary: The University of Chicago Library describes Siddham reaching China around the 6th–7th centuries for Buddhist texts, with later use in Korea and Japan.
events.evidenceNote: Historical connection only; no precise migration path is drawn.
events.sourceLabel: University of Chicago Library · Lineages and Encounters

events.dateLabel: Economic and cultural apogee · 15th–16th centuries CE
events.title: Timbuktu’s manuscript market and Sankore learning centre

languages: Arabic and regional languages · manuscript-specific review required
scripts: Arabic script · for relevant Arabic manuscripts

events.summary: UNESCO describes Timbuktu as a trading crossroads and centre of Islamic learning, with Sankore and manuscript commerce prominent during its 15th–16th-century apogee.
events.evidenceNote: Institutional wording is retained at source level; Sankore is not recast here as a modern-style university without qualification.
events.sourceLabel: UNESCO World Heritage Centre · Timbuktu

events.title: Bologna’s Studium and the medieval university

languages: Latin · major academic language in the period

events.summary: The University of Bologna uses 1088 as the conventionally celebrated foundation date of its Studium and notes its development through student associations.

events.title: Gutenberg Bible printed in Mainz
events.summary: The Library of Congress dates the likely completion of the Gutenberg Bible to late 1455 and identifies it as a Latin Vulgate.

events.title: Arkwright’s water frame patent

events.title: Antarctic Treaty signed
events.summary: The Antarctic Treaty established a framework for peaceful use and scientific cooperation on the continent. It marks modern institutional history, not an ancient settlement record.

events.title: Point-contact transistor demonstrated

events.title: World Wide Web proposed at CERN
events.summary: CERN records Tim Berners-Lee’s March 1989 proposal for an internet-based hypertext system to link and access information across computers.

scriptEvents.title: Ashokan Major Rock Edict site records
scriptEvents.summary: The current atlas records four Major Rock Edict locations—Girnar, Dhauli, Jaugada and Kalsi—as Mauryan-period, 3rd-century BCE site pointers. These points indicate named site records, not a full distribution map.
scriptEvents.evidenceNote: Site-level date and coordinates are retained per record; no inscription transcription or translation is supplied.

scriptEvents.title: Kharoshthi in Aśokan inscriptions
scriptEvents.summary: Unicode’s script history says Kharoshthi first appears in a fully developed form in the Aśokan inscriptions at Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra, dated to around 250 BCE.
scriptEvents.evidenceNote: This is a source-reported attestation, not a claim about the script’s invention date.

scriptEvents.title: Kharoshthi documents in the Tarim Basin
scriptEvents.summary: The British Library and University of Washington project describes birch-bark manuscripts in Gāndhārī written in Kharoshthi and places their language and script in the Gandhāra tradition, current from about the 3rd century BCE to the 4th century CE.
scriptEvents.sourceLabel: University of Washington · British Library Kharoṣṭhī Fragments
scriptEvents.evidenceNote: The event is region-level context; no point coordinate is asserted by this timeline record.

scriptEvents.title: Siddham Buddhist texts reach East Asia
scriptEvents.region: India → China; later Korea and Japan
scriptEvents.summary: The University of Chicago Library describes Siddham reaching China as a script for Buddhist texts around the 6th–7th centuries CE, with later use in Korea and Japan.

scriptEvents.evidenceNote: The timeline shows a reported historical connection, not a route line or a precise migration path.

scriptEvents.title: Southern Brahmic traditions and Southeast Asia
scriptEvents.summary: The University of Chicago Library describes southern Brahmic scripts as influential on Southeast Asian writing systems. The cited page does not assign one date range to this wider lineage, so this record is not placed on the dated axis.
